summary: Mount Konocti Lookout, Lake County: relocated 1977, volunteer watches 2015-2019, closed for safety in October 2019; repairs unfunded as of 2021.

facts.design: Steel X-B tower with a 732-6A cab, similar in design to an Aermotor tower (NHLR gives 45 feet; newspapers give 50 and 75 feet)
facts.status_note: Standing but closed to all access since October 2019 after a Cal Fire inspection found the cab unsafe for occupancy; no source read after 2021 says it was repaired or reopened

staffing.status: volunteers watched from the ground near the tower

access.note: Closed to all access by State officials on October 3, 2019 for safety concerns; no later source read says it reopened

visit.trail_note: Do not climb; the 2019 closure covered all access. The sources read give no drive-up or trail route.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire), which owns the tower

events.note: Moved from an Army receiving station to its current site; NHLR lists 1977 as the build year, but no earlier build date appears in sources read
Registered August 30, 2015 as NHLR US 1104, CA 107
Forest Fire Lookout Association volunteers reopened the tower after 12 years out of service

Cal Fire structural inspection found the wood-framed cab in critical need of repair and unsafe for human occupancy; the association dates the inspection to September 26, the 2019 newspaper to October 3
Closed to all access by State officials on October 3 (association report); the 2019 newspaper says operations were shut down by October 5
Cal Fire said it was willing to sign over responsibility for the lookout repairs to the association
Cal Fire said no money was set aside for lookouts; repairs unfunded and not expected that fire season
Konocti chapter volunteers kept watch from the top of Wright Peak, in the shadow of the tower, May 3 to November 4: 129 days, 1,168 volunteer hours, 18 smoke reports
Cal Fire had not mentioned any concrete repair plans but had told a senator's office the lookout was on its priority list

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 45 feet, the 2019 newspaper 50 feet, and the 2020 newspaper 75 feet. The story reports all three and does not pick one.

The association's 2019 report dates the Cal Fire inspection to September 26 and the closure to all access to October 3. The 2019 newspaper dates the inspection to October 3 and the shutdown to by October 5. The story gives both.

The Register lists 1977 as the build year, but both the Register and the 2020 newspaper describe the 1977 event as relocation to this site from an Army receiving station. The story calls 1977 the relocation year and says no earlier build date appears in the sources read.

notes_for_editor: Height conflicts (45, 50, 75 feet) are reported in the story. Reopening year: the Record-Bee 2019 article says 2015; a Lake County News article dated May 14, 2017, reportedly says June 2016. That page returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text, and a WebFetch summary was used only to learn of the conflict, so no quote from it is used and the story does not cite it. The brief's 2017 solar panel and window repairs, 2018 rotten-wood repair and FFLA grants, 2019 $500 grant, and the August 2015 Cal Fire agreement were not found in any page read, so they are omitted. The Weebly Konocti page has only a header, no history. No source read after 2021 describes the tower's condition or whether repairs or reopening have happened; search snippets from a petition, Facebook posts and a TikTok video were not read and are not used. Photos: the NHLR page has a credit (Photo courtesy of Bill Ulmer) but no image URL, so none added. Budget: 5 distinct pages read (NHLR, Weebly, 2019 and 2021 FFLA reports, two Record-Bee articles) plus one 403 article, against a 6-page budget; 2 web searches used, and one WebFetch used after the 403.
